title: Quantifying training intensity distribution in elite endurance athletes: is there evidence for an “optimal” distribution?
publisher: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
claims: Well-trained junior cross-country skiers adopted a polarized intensity distribution.
About 75% of their training sessions were performed with essentially the entire session below the first ventilatory threshold (2.0 mM blood lactate or less).
In 5-10% of training sessions, major portions of the session were at or near the lactate threshold.
In 15-20% of sessions, training was performed above the second ventilatory threshold, including high-intensity interval work.
